scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which falls just outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Carlos Rodriguez and I'm 29. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello Carlos, I'm sorry to hear about the trouble with your billing while you were traveling. I'd be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide your account number and the email address associated with your subscription?
Sure, my account number is 8849201 and the email is crodriguez@email.com.
Thank you, Carlos. I have located your account. For security, could you please confirm the last four digits of the payment method on file?

Perfect, thank you for verifying. I see the cancellation was processed on day 34. While our 'Subscription Terms of Service' strictly enforce a 30-day window for automatic refunds, I can see your account has been in good standing for three years. I am authorized to make a one-time exception for loyal customers in this situation.
That would be a huge help, thank you so much for understanding my situation.

You're very welcome. I have processed the refund for the full amount of $49.99 back to your card ending in 4492. You should see the credit appear in your bank account within 3-5 business days depending on your financial institution. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

resolution_summary: The agent verified the customer's identity and account status, acknowledged the policy violation, but utilized a discretionary one-time exception for a long-term customer to issue a full refund.
